Interview Experience Report
Amal Verma
Second Year IT

1
Online Assessment

2
Virtual Interview - Round 1
2.1
DSA Questions
2.1.1
Question 1: Make Array Elements Equal
Problem Statement:
Given an array, make all elements equal using the following operations:
• Increment element by one
• Decrement element by one
Follow-up: Increment/decrement cost for each element is different.
Solution Approach:
The optimal solution involves sorting the array and finding the median. I couldn’t immediately think of this approach, so I applied ternary search instead.
Key Learning: The median-based approach provides the optimal solution for minimizing total operations when costs are uniform.
2.1.2
Question 2: Hospital Connectivity
Problem Statement:
Given n cities all connected to each other, with some cities having hospitals. Find the maximum number of roads that can be removed such that hospitals remain accessible from every city.
Follow-up: All cities are not connected - a graph is given.
Solution Approach:
• Method 1: Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) with temporary city
• Method 2: Simple formula approach (as roads are not weighted)
– Total roads - count of non-hospital cities
Analysis: The problem essentially asks for maintaining connectivity while maximizing removals, which translates to finding the minimum edges needed for connectivity.

2.2
Database Management Systems (DBMS)
2.2.1
Normalization Concepts
Topics Covered:
• Definition and importance of normalization
• First Normal Form (1NF) with before/after examples
• Second Normal Form (2NF) with practical examples
• Basic SQL join operations
Example Demonstration:
Provided practical examples showing table structures before and after applying 1NF and 2NF, demonstrating the elimination of redundancy and dependency issues.

3
Virtual Interview - Round 2
3.1
Object-Oriented Programming
3.1.1
Team Management System Design
Problem Statement:
Design a team class with hierarchical structure:
• A team has a manager
• Under manager, there can be reporters or other managers
• Implement two operations:
1. Insert new member to a manager
2. Get the team with highest average rating
Implementation Approach:
Created a hierarchical tree structure with manager-subordinate relationships, implementing recursive algorithms for both insertion and rating calculation operations.

3.2
Data Structures and Algorithms
3.2.1
Range Update Problem
Problem Statement:
Given n queries in format (L, R, C), increment the range L to R by C.
Follow-up: Alternative approach discussion.
Solutions Discussed:
1. Basic Approach: Direct range updates
2. My Approach (standard question): Linear Sweep
3. Advanced Approach (using a datastructure): Lazy Segment Tree for efficient range updates and queries
Implementation Details:
Explained the linear sweep for handling range updates efficiently in O(1) time complexity. Then O(n) post calculation

3.3
Operating Systems
3.3.1
Virtual Memory Management
Topics Covered:
• Virtual RAM concepts
• Page swapping mechanisms
• Page replacement algorithms
3.3.2
LRU Implementation
Problem: Implement Least Recently Used (LRU) cache.
Solution: Double linked list + HashMap approach
• HashMap for O(1) access
• Double linked list for O(1) insertion/deletion
• Maintains order of usage for efficient LRU operations

3.4
Computer Networks
3.4.1
Streaming Architecture
Problem: Design system for streaming to n clients.
Initial Approach: UDP for streaming efficiency.
Congestion Control Challenge:
Since UDP doesn’t support built-in congestion control (unlike TCP), proposed hybrid solution:
• TCP connection: Small packets at fixed intervals for congestion monitoring
• UDP connection: Actual streaming with rate adjustment based on TCP feedback
• Dynamic stream rate adjustment based on congestion detection
3.4.2
Website Performance Issues
Scenario: Website loads fine locally but slow for friend in Lucknow.
Potential Causes Identified:
1. Network Issues: Bandwidth limitations, latency problems
2. Infrastructure: Network line capacity constraints
3. DNS Issues: Domain resolution overhead and delays
4. CDN Problems: Content Delivery Network configuration or availability
3.4.3
CDN Deep Dive
CDN (Content Delivery Network):
• Described distributed system architecture
• Explained edge server concepts and geographic optimization
• Discussed caching strategies and content synchronization

3.5
Database Systems - Advanced
3.5.1
Stored Procedure Concurrency
Scenario: Stored procedure for transferring amount X from account A to account B
• Query 1: Decrement from account A
• Query 2: Increment to account B
Concurrency Issues Identified:
• Race conditions between concurrent transactions
• Potential for inconsistent states
• Data integrity concerns
Solution - Row Locking:
Implemented row-level locking to ensure transaction atomicity and consistency.
Follow-up - Deadlock Prevention:
• Deadlock Scenario: Multiple transactions waiting for each other’s locks
• Prevention Strategies:
– Consistent lock ordering
– Timeout mechanisms
– Deadlock detection and resolution algorithms

3.6
C++ Programming Concepts
3.6.1
Memory Management
Topics Covered:
• Pointer operations and memory allocation
• Struct size calculations and memory alignment

4
Project Discussion
4.1
Real-time Collaborative IDE
Project Overview:
Developed a collaborative integrated development environment enabling multiple users to code simultaneously in real-time.
Key Features Implemented:
• Real-time code synchronization
• Multi-user editing capabilities
• Conflict resolution mechanisms
• User session management
Technical Implementation:
• WebSocket connections for real-time communication
• Operational Transform algorithms for conflict resolution
• Version control integration
• Scalable backend architecture
Concurrency Challenges:
• Problem: Multiple users editing same code sections simultaneously
• Solution: Implemented operational transform with priority-based conflict resolution
• Additional Measures: User locks on critical code sections, visual indicators for concurrent edits
Potential Improvements:
• Enhanced conflict resolution algorithms
• Better user experience with visual collaboration indicators
• Performance optimization for large codebases
• Integration with popular version control systems

5
Interview Reflection
5.1
Technical Performance
• Successfully demonstrated problem-solving approaches across multiple domains
• Showed depth in both theoretical understanding and practical implementation
• Effectively communicated complex technical concepts
• Adapted solutions based on follow-up questions and constraints
5.2
Areas of Strength
• Strong foundation in data structures and algorithms
• Good understanding of system design principles
• Ability to think through trade-offs and alternative approaches
• Clear communication of technical concepts
5.3
Learning Points
• Importance of considering multiple solution approaches
• Value of understanding underlying principles rather than just memorizing solutions
• Significance of discussing trade-offs and edge cases
• Need for practical implementation knowledge alongside theoretical understanding
5.4
Key Takeaways
1. Preparation Strategy: Balanced focus on fundamentals across all core computer science subjects
2. Problem-Solving Approach: Think aloud, consider multiple solutions, discuss trade-offs
3. Communication: Clear explanation of thought process and implementation details
4. Adaptability: Ability to pivot and explore alternative approaches based on interviewer feedback
This interview experience provided valuable insights into the technical depth expected in software engineering interviews and highlighted the importance of strong fundamentals across multiple domains.
